newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Foreign buying fuels early rise in Singapore stock.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying fuels early rise in Singapore stock.

text.p: Keen foreign interest on selected blue chips pushed the key Straits Times Industrials (STI) Index up at mid-morning on Wednesday, dealers said.
"There is good interest seen from foreign funds on selected stocks, mainly the banking stocks," said a dealer with a European institution.
At 0230 GMT, the index was up 16.81 points, at 2,213.86, led by Keppel Corp and Fraser & Neave, up Singapore S$0.20 (US$0.14) each. Foreign tranches of OCBC, DBS and UOB rose S$0.50 each.
Turnover was active, around 145 million shares, with gainers outpacing losers by 264 to 70.
Malaysian shares like Sri Hartamas and MBf Holdings hogged the actives on keen retail and speculative interest.

Dealers said Sri Hartamas was benefiting from interest in MBf Holdings, a shareholder of the property firm. About 233,000 of the 13 million shares in Sri Hartamas were crossed at S$1.18 to $1.22. MBf saw over 7.1 million shares traded.
Warrants of Liang Huat and Jack Chia were top percentage gainers, rising over 18.5 and 15.2 percent respectively.
Thai Fund and Clipsal led losers, shedding US$0.20 and S$0.12 respectively on thin volumes.
